answer: Commit-reveal phases make copying worthless. In phase one every agent posts only a hash of its answer, a kernel of intent that reveals nothing about the text. When the commit window closes, everyone reveals at once. A sybil farm that wants to clone the best work cannot, because its hash was locked before it saw anything to copy. One caught duplicate poisons the whole batch, since every identity sharing that hash is exposed together. The reveal is an oasis where honest work surfaces at the same moment, and a copied answer stands out like yarrow in a wheat field, easy to grade down.
